newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lambasts Swiss envoy comments on Holocaust.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lambasts Swiss envoy comments on Holocaust.

text.p: The United States on Monday lambasted the Swiss ambassador for urging his government to wage a public relations campaign against American Jewish groups seeking compensation for Holocaust victims.

"If it's true the Swiss ambassador made these remarks it betrays a fundamental lack of understanding of the commitment the United States government has to its own citizens and of the search for justice for people who had their human rights fundamentally violated during the Second World War. It is very troubling," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

Swiss Ambassador to the United States Carlo Jagmetti resigned on Monday in an uproar over a confidential document he wrote calling for "waging war" against Jewish groups and other critics. The comments were in a strategy paper he sent to Berne last month on how to handle a dispute over dormant accounts of Hitler's victims in Swiss banks.

Burns said he hoped the quotes were not accurate "because any ambassador in Washington who advocates waging a public relations campaign against American Jewish groups and against Holocaust survivors is just wrong-headed. It's just not the right thing to do."

In addition to Jewish groups, critics have included Republican Sen. Alfonse D'Amato of New York, who has accused the Swiss of profiting cynically from the war. Burns vigorously defended D'Amato, saying he was "doing the Lord's work" and that the Clinton administration "fully supports" his efforts to "get to the bottom of this question."

"Senator D'Amato is representing a group of people in the United States who either personally were victims of the Holocaust or whose close family members were, who have a reason to expect that the Swiss government will undertake an objective and fully comprehensive study of what happened to the funds and personal finances of Holocaust victims before, during and after the Second World War," Burns said.
D'Amato called Jagmetti's resignation "appropriate" and added, "Now it is essential for the Swiss government to repudiate the chilling remarks made by the ambassador."

The State Department has undertaken its own study to establish what the U.S. government knew or did not know in the years following the war. Burns said this review would be completed in a couple of weeks.
He said he did not believe the United States applied pressure to have the ambassador resign, adding: "I think it's a unilateral Swiss decision."

After months of international criticism Switzerland last week agreed in principle to establish a compensation fund for Holocaust victims. Burns welcomed this move as "an important first step in coming to terms with the past."
